**The History of Tea: From Ancient China to the World**

Tea, one of the world's most beloved beverages, has a rich and storied history that spans thousands of years. Its journey from ancient China to成为全球性饮料的故事，reflects not only trade routes and cultural exchanges but also the evolution of human civilization itself.

The origins of tea can be traced back to ancient China, where legend attributes its discovery to Emperor Shen Nung around 2737 BCE. According to folklore, while boiling water over an open fire, dried leaves from a nearby tree accidentally fell into his pot, creating the first infusion. Whether myth or history, this moment marked the beginning of tea's remarkable legacy. Early Chinese texts from the Han Dynasty (206 BCE – 220 CE) already documented tea's medicinal properties and its use in religious ceremonies by Buddhist monks to maintain alertness during meditation.

During the Tang Dynasty (618–907 CE), tea culture flourished under Emperor Taizong, who promoted its cultivation. Lu Yu's "The Classic of Tea" (Cha Jing), written around 800 CE, became the first comprehensive treatise on tea cultivation and preparation. This period saw tea transition from a medicinal herb to a sophisticated beverage enjoyed by scholars, poets, and emperors alike. The Song Dynasty (960–1279 CE) further refined tea culture, with the development of powdered green tea whisked into frothy drinks that remain popular in Japan today.

Tea's journey beyond China began during the Tang Dynasty when Buddhist monks carried it to Japan. Japanese monks like Eisai introduced tea cultivation to their homeland in the 12th century, where it became integrated into Zen Buddhist practice. By the Ming Dynasty (1368–1644 CE), loose-leaf tea replaced powdered forms, and tea began spreading along maritime trade routes to Southeast Asia, India, and beyond.

The global expansion of tea accelerated during the Age of Discovery. Portuguese traders encountered Chinese tea in the 16th century, followed by Dutch merchants who established trading posts in Asia.
